## What it is

The cup grille: an 86 (X) x 94 (Y) plate, 2.5 thick, vertical corners chamfered 4 mm, centred on the tower axis. The long side follows the chimney's lens (tips toward ±Y), so the grille only drops into the outer grille's 90 x 98 cut-out the right way round or turned half a turn, which is the same grille; turned a quarter, its 94 meets the cut-out's 90. Under it a seat boss (with two flush Ø8 x 3 strong magnet wells) that drops into the tower's top socket, and a lens-shaped drip ring (1.6 wall, down to Z 43) around the chimney's top. Solid over the ring, rows of drain slots from the ring to the border, two Ø16 finger holes on one diagonal. Modelled in the machine frame and returned through `scale_flip(scale_frame(...))`: it prints top face down, the top face on the bed. Bambu PETG Basic.

## Design notes

- Modelled in the machine frame and ends with `scale_frame` then `scale_flip` (it prints top face down).
- Drip ring: `scale_lens` of the chimney's outer face (kerb lens grown by the tube wall: body 24.6, tip 5.6) grown by `drip_ring_clearance` 2.5, so inner face body 27.1 / tip 8.1 (reaches 34.97 along Y), outer face 28.7 / 9.7 (36.57 along Y). The chimney's grip shrinks the real tube by 0.1, so the gap is 2.55 in practice.
- The solid zone is whatever the slots leave: about Ø58 across X and the diagonals, out to about 37.6 along Y at the lens tips. Smallest cup 60 mm across, so the solid is not there for the cups but to shield the chimney.
- Slots: rows parallel to each side, laid out by `_slot_layout`. First row 3 mm from the edge, then inward at a pitch of `slot_width + slot_web` (5.5) while any row still has room. A slot's centre line keeps clear of the ring's outer face by 1 mm, of the finger holes by 2.5 mm, of the plate edge (corner chamfers included) by 3 mm, and of the 45° diagonal from each plate corner by half a web: the diagonal splits the east-west rows from the north-south ones. Runs shorter than 2 x slot_width are dropped, longer than `max_slot_length` (25) are split with a web. The finger hole clearance is applied at all four corners, so the slot layout is mirror symmetric in X and Y.
- Default result: 26 slots, 3 rows east and west (X ±38.5, ±33, ±27.5), 3 rows north and south (Y ±42.5, ±37, ±31.5), split around the lens tips. About 1230 mm² of slots, plus 400 for the finger holes (260 + 400 with the earlier single row).
- Finger holes: `finger_hole_border` 4 of solid to both edges of their corner, so centres at (±31, ∓35) from the axis.
- Every slot is at least 5.1 mm from the chimney's outer face (1 + 1.6 + 2.5), so water through a slot falls outside it.
- Checked in `scale_assembly`: clean (no shared volume with the tower or the chimney).
- The magnets' skin to the plate's top face is 2.5 mm; the boss flank is 0.99 mm from each well at the boss's lower face.
- Chamfer 1 on the plate's underside outline, done on the plain plate before the boss, ring and cuts are added. Nothing on the top face (bed after the flip).
- One `min_wall` warning (0.59 mm) sits on a corner of the seat boss, where two 30° flanks meet in a sharp ridge: the check measures the ridge's tip, not a wall. The boss is 20.5 mm across at its narrow end.

## Don't

- Do not put an opening inside the drip ring's outer face, nor within 1 mm of it: the solid over the ring shields the chimney.
- Do not go back to a round ring and solid: the lens frees about 8 mm of band on X and the diagonals, the round one only fits the lens tips.
- Do not make the plate square again: the rectangle is what stops it going in a quarter turn off. The difference between its sides has to stay over 4 mm (2 mm gap per side in the cut-out).
- Do not chamfer the top face, the boss flanks or the wells.
- Do not break the mirror symmetry of the slots; the finger holes are the only asymmetry, and the part is the same after half a turn.
- Do not remove the final `scale_frame`: without it the part prints as its mirror image (found 2026-11-16: the PCB box came out on the wrong side of the cell).
